name: Two-Stage Inverse Rendering Optimization
aliases: Hybrid Differentiable Rendering for Inverse Rendering
definition: A two-stage optimization pipeline that first optimizes geometry using an approximate differentiable renderer (Silhouette-based) and then optimizes reflectance (diffuse/specular albedo) using a physically-based differentiable renderer (Ray-tracing).
summary: Two-Stage Inverse Rendering Optimization decouples geometry and material recovery using distinct renderers to explicitly reconstruct triangle meshes and PBR materials for direct graphics engine deployment.
